title: Single Nuclei Extraction from Frozen Brain
author: Neurogenomics And Informatics
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2a5gag6
materials: Tricine-KOH is 17.92 grams Tricine (Sigma T0377) and 100 mL RNAse free water for 1 M solution (pH to 7.8 with KOH as needed. Usually takes about 3-4 mL of 3M KOH).
Recipe:___________ commercial PBS (46-013CM 10x PBS from Corning)
For Beckman put in swing-out rotor (S0410).
Prepare working concentrations of rest of solutions.
Nuclei should be pelleted at the bottom

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Safety
steps.instruction: Set up the workspace and equipment according to BSL2 precautions.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves, a disposable gown, and a mask if working outside a hood.
Wash all surfaces and reusable equipment (homogenizers, centrifuge tubes) with 25% bleach.
Prepare 10% bleach for sterilization of supernatants and tissue byproducts.
Turn on Beckman Allegra 64R and Eppendorf 5430R centrifuges to reach 4°C.
Set acceleration and deceleration to 0 on the Beckman centrifuge.

steps.title: Prepare Homogenization Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare the homogenization medium (6 ml per sample + ~2 ml extra for 30% Iodixanol).

substeps.instruction: For 100 ml (or 50 ml) recipe: combine 5 mM MgCl2 (0.5 ml or 0.25 ml of 1M stock), 20 mM Tricine-KOH (2 ml or 1 ml of 1M stock), and bring to volume with RNAse free ddH2O.
Supplement the medium with 0.15 mM spermine (1 µl per 10 ml), 0.5 mM spermidine (1 µl per 10 ml), and an EDTA-free protease inhibitor tablet.
If using for RNA, add 1 µl RNASIN per ml of medium.
Prepare 35% Iodixanol: Mix 7 ml 50% Iodixanol with 3 ml supplemented homogenization medium (for 4 samples, use 12 mL of 50% Iodixanol and 5.14 mL supplemented homogenization buffer).
Prepare 50% Iodixanol stock: Mix 5 volumes 60% Optiprep stock with 1 volume dilutant (e.g., 17.5 ml stock to 3.5 ml diluant for 4 samples).

steps.title: Homogenize Brain Tissue
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt the brain tissue to release nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 2 ml of supplemented homogenization medium per 15 ml Kontes glass homogenizer tube (suitable for 1g of tissue).
Place brain sample on ice in the 2 ml medium.
Homogenize with 10 strokes using 'A' pestle and 10 strokes using 'B' pestle on ice.
Verify that no large pieces of tissue remain.
Transfer the homogenate using a 2 ml strippette into two 2 ml siliconized snap cap microcentrifuge tubes.
Rinse the glass homogenizer with an additional 500 µl of supplemented homogenization buffer and transfer the remaining homogenate to the microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Initial Pelleting and Cleaning
steps.instruction: Remove debris and concentrate the nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Spin tubes at 500 RCF for 5 minutes at 4°C in the Eppendorf centrifuge.
Pour off supernatant (optionally freeze 100 µl at -80°C for cytoplasmic RNA analysis).
Resuspend the pellet by adding 1 ml supplemented homogenization medium and flicking/turning the tube.
Resuspend each pellet in 700 µl supplemented homogenization buffer and combine all tubes for one sample into a single 15 ml conical tube.

steps.title: Density Gradient Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Separate nuclei from myelin and debris using an Iodixanol gradient.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 ml of 35% Iodixanol to a polycarbonate Beckman Coulter centrifuge tube for each sample; mix and spin briefly if necessary to settle the solution.
Add an equal volume of 50% Iodixanol to the sample in the 15 ml conical to create a final 25% Iodixanol concentration.
Carefully layer ~3-4 ml of the 25% Iodixanol sample on top of the 4 ml of 35% Iodixanol by pipetting slowly against the tube wall.
Centrifuge at 10,000 rpm (top speed) for 30 minutes in the Beckman Allegra (ensure acceleration/deceleration are set to 0).
Remove the top pink myelin debris layer using a transfer pipette.
Vacuum up the nuclei from the interface (cloudy layer) using a low retention pipette and transfer to non-stick 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes (max 500 µl per tube).

steps.title: Nuclei Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the extracted nuclei to remove Iodixanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml supplemented Nuclei Wash buffer to the tubes, mix, and centrifuge at 500g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend nuclei in ~750 µl Nuclei Wash buffer; combine all nuclei for one sample into a single tube.
Centrifuge at 500g at 4°C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend nuclei in ~1000 µl Nuclei Wash buffer, centrifuge at 500g at 4°C, and discard supernatant.
Perform a final resuspension in ~1000 µl Nuclei Wash buffer.

steps.title: Final Filtration and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Filter the nuclei and verify concentration and quality.

substeps.instruction: Pass the nuclei through a 40 µm Nylon mesh cell strainer (#229481) to remove clumps.
Take 20 µl of the suspension, mix 1:1 with 1:2000 DAPI solution, and count using a hemacytometer or Countess to check for clumps.
Adjust the nuclei aliquot to a final dilution of 1,200 cells per µl and re-count to confirm.

steps.title: Storage
steps.instruction: Store remaining nuclei for future use.

substeps.instruction: Pellet the remaining nuclei and resuspend in 100% methanol.
